exposure: Prenatal nicotine exposure (2 mg/kg per day nicotine bitartrate from days 26-160)
Maternal vitamin C supplementation (ascorbic acid at 50, 100, or 250 mg/kg per day)
outcome: Placental hemodynamics (placental volume blood flow, maternal placental blood flow)
Placental histology (villous cytotrophoblast cell islands, syncytiotrophoblast sprouting)
cohort: Time-mated macaques (n=27) divided into control, nicotine only, vitamin C only, and nicotine plus vitamin C treatment groups.
finding: Prenatal nicotine exposure significantly decreased fetal blood supply via reduced placental volume blood flow and increased villous cytotrophoblast cell islands and syncytiotrophoblast sprouting, all of which were mitigated by vitamin C supplementation.
gest_age: Prenatal development up to near-term delivery (160 days, with term being 168 days).
